page.layout: Two printed pages on the scan. Left page: only a cut-off strip of its outer column at the left edge, with hyphenated line ends and no legible continuous text. Right page: running head at top with page number, one text column of two paragraphs, marginal notes in the right margin, and a line at the foot ending in "Au-" with "1 5" beside it.

main_text.p: Cyprianus sic docet: lib. de Baptism. Christi. a Legat hic vnum verbum, & in hoc mandato meditatur Christiana religio: & iuuenies ex hac Scriptura omnium doctrinarum regulam emanasse, & huc nasci, & hinc reuerti, quicquid Ecclesiasticè ventilatum disputata [?].

Optatus eandem doctrinam refulit: lib.5. b Nemo vobis credas, nemo [?] sumus, omnes sententiosi homines sumus. Quaerendi sunt iudices. Si Christiani de utraque parte dari non possunt, quia sanguis veritas imputatur. De foro quae ratio est iudex: si paganus, non potest nosse Christiana mysteria; si Iudaeus, inimicus est Christiani baptismatis. Ergo in terris de hac re nullam potestis reperire iudicium: de caelo quaerendum est iudex. Sed ad quid cultum adeo ad caelum, cum habemus hic in Evangelio? Haec ille. Iesuitae nostri hunc sanctum Patrem vel caecum fuisse dicent, vel delirum senem, vel indoctum, vel invidum Papae detractatorem, qui quum de iudice controversiarum ex professo disputaret, tanto se labore fatigans quaerendo, nec tamen hunc iudicem in terris inuenerit. At quam facile Papam controversiarum iudicem pronunciare potuisset, si illum iudicem Ecclesia tunc agnouisset? Haec Iesuitas doler, quod Papam penitus exclauserit. Exclusit omnino, quum in terris iudicem controversiarum de fide inveniri nullum posse profiteatur. Sensum Ecclesiae illius saeculi magna fide refert Optatus, Papam non habitum fuisse Christi in terris Vicarium, non iudicem controversiarum, non caput, non os Ecclesiae. Haec sunt recentia fratrum figmenta, antiquis Patribus inaudita monstra. 1 5 Au-

page.notes: The page is heavily shadowed by a dark stain across the centre of the right page, and the left-hand strip is cut off at the scan edge. Readings in the middle of the right column are doubtful and are marked [?] where I could not confirm them letter by letter; several words may be wrong. The left strip is not legible enough to transcribe, so each visible line end is given as illegible. The page number is printed as "II5" and is kept as printed. The "1 5" beside "Au-" at the foot is unclear and may be a signature or a stray mark; it is kept in the text. Marginal notes on the right: "lib. de Baptism. Christi." (reference a) and "lib.5." (reference b). The reference marks a and b in the text are not clearly visible and are placed where the notes stand.
